childSafety.title: Child Safety Standards of THERS Social Network
childSafety.intro: THERS Social Network has zero tolerance for child sexual exploitation and abuse. This content is prohibited on our platform, without exceptions.
childSafety.prohibitedIntro: It is prohibited to post, share, request or facilitate any of the following content or conduct:
prohibited: Grooming: approaching a minor to gain their trust for sexual purposes.
Sexual requests or proposals directed at minors.
Distributing, offering or linking to this kind of content.
Generated or manipulated content that depicts minors in a sexual way.
childSafety.reportIntro: In the THERS app you can report posts, comments, messages you have received and accounts:
reportSteps: Open the “⋯” menu of the content or conversation.
Select the category “Child exploitation or abuse”.
Send the report. You may add a detail if you wish.
childSafety.reportAnonymous: The reported person will not know who sent the report.
childSafety.handlingTitle: What we do with these reports
handling: Reports in this category receive top-priority review.
Content of this kind can be removed immediately.
Accounts may be suspended when appropriate.
childSafety.sensitiveTitle: Sensitive content and prohibited content are not the same
childSafety.sensitiveAllowed: Permitted sensitive content may be shown with a warning or blur once THERS implements that mechanism.
childSafety.sensitiveForbidden: Child exploitation or abuse content is not “sensitive content”: it is prohibited and can be removed immediately.
age: THERS is exclusively for people aged 18 or older.
If there are reasonable grounds to believe an account belongs to a person under 18, THERS may restrict it and request age verification.
childSafety.contactWarning: Do not send or forward illegal material by email. This address is a contact channel; the primary reporting mechanism is the THERS reporting system.
childSafety.legal: THERS complies with the applicable child safety legislation and cooperates with the competent authorities when there is a valid legal obligation to do so.
